cards.title: PAC-learning hardness versus natural-proof barriers under universality
cards.formal: Assume the Universality Conjecture U for succinct pseudorandom generators defined below. Is LIH equivalent to NN? LIH says that polynomial-size Boolean circuits are not efficiently learnable in the distribution-free, realizable, improper PAC model using labeled examples only. More precisely, for some fixed integer k≥1 there is no probabilistic polynomial-time learner for all n-input circuits of size at most n^k under every input distribution. NN says that for every real 0<α<1 there is no nonuniform polynomial-in-truth-table-size natural property useful against circuits of size at most ⌊2^{αn}⌋. Thus the requested proposition is U ⇒ (LIH ⇔ NN), with all three assertions and their computational conventions specified here.
cards.why: Would identify whether ordinary PAC-learning hardness belongs to the same conditional complexity picture as barriers to recognizing hard Boolean functions, beyond the membership-query learning equivalence already known under universality.
cards.status_note: Read the full primary definitions and concluding question, the exact cited LIH assumption and learning model, and the 2025 learning-hardness result’s model distinctions. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution of this particular conditional equivalence. Uniformity, query access, arbitrary distributions and natural-property size scale are preserved explicitly.

sentences: The question assumes a universal construction of succinct pseudorandom generators whenever suitable succinct distributions exist.
It asks whether ordinary distribution-free improper PAC-learning hardness is then equivalent to the absence of the specified natural properties.
The learner receives random labeled examples and must work for every distribution without a sampler description.
Natural properties are tested on complete truth tables and must reject every sufficiently small circuit while accepting at least half of all functions.
The source already proves a related equivalence with membership-query access under the uniform distribution, which is a different learning model.

cards.definitions:
Circuits are finite acyclic Boolean circuits over fan-in-two AND and OR and unary NOT, with constants and unrestricted reuse; size counts gates. SIZE[s(n)] denotes functions on n bits with such circuits of size at most s(n). Circuit descriptions list gates and wire indices. A truth table tt(f) lists the 2^n values of f in lexicographic input order. Write N=2^n and U_j for the uniform distribution on j-bit strings. Polynomial size for a test of a truth table means polynomial in N, not in n.

PAC model: for a fixed k, an efficient learner is one uniform probabilistic oracle Turing machine A_k with a fixed polynomial time bound in n,1/ε,1/δ. Given 1^n and rational 0<ε,δ<1, it can request independent samples (x,f(x)), where x has any distribution D on {0,1}^n and f∈SIZE[n^k]. The cost includes processing the n-bit samples and writing the output; a sample request itself is available as an oracle operation. No description or efficient sampler for D is promised. For every n,f,D,ε,δ it must output a circuit h such that Pr_{x∼D}[h(x)≠f(x)]≤ε with probability at least 1−δ over the learner’s coins and all examples. The output circuit may be larger than n^k and need not lie in the target size class; its size is bounded by the learner’s time. The target labels are noiseless, so this is realizable learning, not agnostic learning. The learner has no membership-query oracle for chosen x. LIH is the negation of the assertion that such an A_k exists for every fixed k, allowing its time polynomial to depend on k.

Natural properties: for a fixed α, a property is a sequence R_n of sets of Boolean functions on n bits. It is natural and useful against SIZE[⌊2^{αn}⌋] if (a) there is a nonuniform family of Boolean tests B_n of size (2^n)^{O(1)} deciding f∈R_n from tt(f); (b) for every sufficiently large n, at least half of all 2^{2^n} Boolean functions belong to R_n; and (c) for every sufficiently large n, no function in SIZE[⌊2^{αn}⌋] belongs to R_n. The size exponent is fixed across n but may depend on the property. NN forbids every such property for each fixed 0<α<1. This uses the source’s density-1/2 convention and nonuniform constructivity.

Universality U: for every fixed 0<α<1, there exist a seed-length function K_α(N)<N and one uniform algorithm G_α, running in N^{O(1)} time on (1^N,s) with s∈{0,1}^{K_α(N)}, with the following implication. If there is any sequence of distributions μ_N over N-bit truth tables supported on functions in SIZE[⌊N^α⌋] that fools all polynomial-size Boolean tests with negligible advantage, then G_α(1^N,U_{K_α(N)}) is also such a succinct pseudorandom distribution. No efficient sampling assumption is imposed on μ_N. For G_α, every output for every seed must be a truth table of a circuit of size at most ⌊N^α⌋. Here N ranges over powers of two, and the requirements are asymptotic in N. To fool all polynomial-size tests with negligible advantage means that for every fixed a,b>0 and all sufficiently large N, every test B of size at most N^a satisfies |Pr_{y∼μ_N}[B(y)=1]−Pr_{y∼U_N}[B(y)=1]|≤N^{−b}; the same definition applies to generator outputs. This is the default polynomial-time, nonuniform-security version of Definition 6 and Conjecture 19, rather than its separately defined nonuniform-generator variant.
cards.answer_criterion: Prove the conditional equivalence U ⇒ (LIH ⇔ NN), or refute that implication with its stated quantifiers. A positive resolution must establish both directions under U for distribution-free realizable improper PAC learning from examples and the specified natural-property barrier. Establishing only the source’s uniform-distribution membership-query equivalence, restricting hypothesis size, assuming a sampler for the example distribution, or using an agnostic-learning NP-hardness hypothesis does not settle this formulation.

context_blocks.title: The learning assumption named in the question
context_blocks.text: Applebaum, Barak and Xiao’s LIH assumption concerns learning polynomial-size circuits from labeled examples under arbitrary distributions, allowing any efficiently evaluable hypothesis. The distribution is not supplied by a circuit whose complexity can be charged to the learner.

context_blocks.title: What universality connects
context_blocks.text: The Universality Conjecture asks for a uniform succinct generator whenever suitable succinct pseudorandom distributions exist, even if those distributions have no known efficient sampler. Under it, the source proves equivalences between natural-property barriers, pseudorandomness and several forms of computational hardness.

context_blocks.title: The known learning equivalence has different access
context_blocks.text: Theorem 22 already covers hardness of learning polynomial-size circuits with membership queries under the uniform input distribution. Its concluding question separately names ordinary LIH. The two learning tasks must remain distinct in the card.

context_blocks.title: The natural-property scale
context_blocks.text: The formal theorem uses polynomial-size tests of full truth tables, density at least one half and usefulness against 2^{αn}-size circuits for every fixed positive α below one. Replacing that target by a vague absence of circuit lower-bound arguments would lose its computational content.

context_blocks.title: Later learning hardness is more specific
context_blocks.text: Goldberg and Kabanets’s 2025 paper relates witness encryption to specified NP-hardness reductions for a computational gap-learning problem. Its unconditional Boolean-circuit result restricts hypothesis size and is agnostic; other improper results change the computational model. These do not establish the conditional equivalence for the realizable distribution-free model stated here.

cards.context:
Applebaum, Barak and Xiao’s LIH assumption concerns learning polynomial-size circuits from labeled examples under arbitrary distributions, allowing any efficiently evaluable hypothesis. The distribution is not supplied by a circuit whose complexity can be charged to the learner.

The Universality Conjecture asks for a uniform succinct generator whenever suitable succinct pseudorandom distributions exist, even if those distributions have no known efficient sampler. Under it, the source proves equivalences between natural-property barriers, pseudorandomness and several forms of computational hardness.

Theorem 22 already covers hardness of learning polynomial-size circuits with membership queries under the uniform input distribution. Its concluding question separately names ordinary LIH. The two learning tasks must remain distinct in the card.

The formal theorem uses polynomial-size tests of full truth tables, density at least one half and usefulness against 2^{αn}-size circuits for every fixed positive α below one. Replacing that target by a vague absence of circuit lower-bound arguments would lose its computational content.

Goldberg and Kabanets’s 2025 paper relates witness encryption to specified NP-hardness reductions for a computational gap-learning problem. Its unconditional Boolean-circuit result restricts hypothesis size and is agnostic; other improper results change the computational model. These do not establish the conditional equivalence for the realizable distribution-free model stated here.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
